chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from a man who narrated to him, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about three persons who were on a journey: one of them was in janābah, the second was dead, and the third was without wudu (ablution). The time of salat (prayer) arrived, and they had with them only enough water for one of them. Who should take the water and perform ghusl with it, and what should they do?

He said: "The person in janābah should perform ghusl, the deceased should be buried, and the one who requires wudu (ablution) should perform tayammum, because ghusl for janābah is an obligation, washing the dead is sunnah (prophetic tradition), and tayammum is permissible for the other."

What this hadith contains, namely that washing the dead is sunnah (prophetic tradition), does not conflict with what we have stated, for several reasons. One of them is that this report is mursal, because Ibn Abī Najrān said, "from a man," and did not name him, and it is possible that he was neither trusted nor reliable. Then even if it were authentic, the intent in attributing this ghusl to the sunnah (prophetic tradition) would be that its obligation became known through the sunnah (prophetic tradition), because the Qur'an does not indicate the obligation of washing the dead; rather, we only came to know it through the sunnah (prophetic tradition). We have previously cited the narration of Yūnus from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, that he said: "Among the ghusls, three are obligatory." Then he mentioned among them washing the dead, and we have already discussed this report earlier.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: Dry ablution used as a lawful substitute when water cannot be used.
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: The Qur'an, invoked here as a source not explicitly indicating this ruling.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of janābah requiring ghusl.
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: That which is established through the sunnah (prophetic tradition); here discussed in legal usage.
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْمَيِّتِ: The ritual washing of the deceased.
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: A report with a disconnected or incomplete sanad/isnad (chain of narrators).

ai.seo_question: When water is only enough for one person, should it be used for ghusl of janābah, washing the dead, or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report discusses a legal ruling for a case of limited water during travel involving a person in janābah, a deceased person, and another without wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام prioritizes ghusl for janābah, while the compiler then explains that the description of washing the dead as sunnah (prophetic tradition) does not negate its obligation, since that obligation is established through the sunnah (prophetic tradition), and he also notes a weakness in the report's sanad/isnad (chain of narrators).
